meta.title: ContextWatchdog · redact in place before you paste, without your data leaving the machine
meta.description: Open-source, free and backend-free local redaction for AI workflows: detects and replaces secrets and personal data before text reaches a model. A browser extension today; desktop, CLI and proxy planned.

hero.badge: Open source · Free · No server · No account
hero.title: Redact in place, before you paste
hero.subtitle: Before you paste a config, a log, a ticket or a stack trace into an AI, ContextWatchdog finds the secrets and personal data inside it and replaces them with placeholders in place. Detection and replacement happen entirely on your device — the text never leaves it.

demo.title: 30 seconds
demo.caption: Paste a config containing a database password: the original text is inserted normally first (input is never blocked), then replaced **in place** with placeholders once detection finishes, with a brief "3 redactions" toast in the corner. Nothing interrupts what you were doing.

cases.label: Config & secrets
cases.note: Placeholders stay semantic, so the redacted config is still understandable to the AI.

cases.label: Everyday text · General profile
cases.original: Customer service notes: phone 13812345678, ID 11010519491231002X, card 6222021202021234563, email zhang.wei@example.com — ticket synced.
cases.redacted: Customer service notes: phone <<PHONE>>, ID <<ID_CARD>>, card <<CARD_NUMBER>>, email zhang.wei@example.com — ticket synced.
cases.note: Phone, ID and bank card are replaced in place; the email stays put per the built-in default — redacted by your rules, not blindly.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Three steps from detection to destination — all on-device: offline, silent, and every change reversible.

steps.title: Heuristic recognition
steps.body: Targets with a fixed shape — secrets, phone numbers, national IDs, bank cards, emails, IPs, plates — are found by shape heuristics plus algorithmic validation (checksums, area segments, character distributions); a hit is trusted. Recognition runs on your device: no network, no text goes to any service.

steps.title: In-place replacement
steps.body: A value repeated N times, or spans that overlap, are merged by one sharing pass: every occurrence becomes the same placeholder, and overlaps are arbitrated by type priority. Placeholders stay semantic — <<PHONE>> still reads as what it is, so the redacted text stays readable and inferable.

steps.title: Silent, wherever you paste
steps.body: The redacted text lands directly in your paste target: the chat window receives the redacted version. The whole pass is otherwise silent, with only one brief “N redactions” toast; any row can be switched on the spot from “replace” to “keep” — whether to let that item through unchanged remains your call.

engine.title: Detection engine
engine.lead: Two tiers share one dedupe and arbitration pass: the regex tier handles fixed shapes, the AI tier covers shapeless entities; both are extensible through your custom profiles.

tiers.title: Regex tier (always on, extensible)
tiers.body: Secrets, phone numbers, national IDs, bank cards, emails, IPs and plates — targets with a fixed shape — are matched by regex plus algorithmic validation. A match is trusted: zero latency, fully offline. Beyond the built-in 14 categories, a custom profile lets you add regex rules, adjust defaults and keep an allowlist — coverage is yours.

tiers.title: AI tier (optional)
tiers.body: Entities with no fixed shape — names, addresses — go to a local GLiNER model (WASM), which only looks at spans the regex tier left uncovered and never redoes its work; you must enable it explicitly and download the quantized model once (~183 MB). If the model is unavailable, the pipeline degrades to pure regex: no errors, no blocking.

engine.note: Note: limited by model size, AI enhancement does not reliably recognise some general Chinese text; fixed-shape targets — phone, ID, bank card and email — remain handled by the always-on regex tier, and multilingual support is on the roadmap.

privacy.title: Verifiable privacy claims
privacy.lead: Every row below can be checked in this repository — you do not have to take our word for it.

items.claim: The extension never sends your text to a server
items.how: Exactly two fetch calls exist in the repository, both in modelDownload.ts, both used only to download the model — no request ever carries your text. No XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket or EventSource anywhere; storage is chrome.storage.local only with no cloud sync, and your text stays in on-device memory throughout.

items.claim: The only network activity: optional model download
items.how: The AI tier is off by default; only when you enable it are model files downloaded and cached from whitelisted hosts (a ModelScope mirror, falling back to huggingface.co). Only those two addresses are whitelisted; only model files are downloaded, never any of your data. Caching and inference stay on-device, so it still works offline.

The manifest declares no content_scripts and no <all_urls>, only optional_host_permissions: injection is on demand, so only sites on your authorised list receive the paste listener and widget. Unauthorised sites get zero listeners and zero DOM probing. Removing a site clears its settings, and the widget mounts only in the top document.

items.claim: No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting
items.how: There is no analytics, reporting or telemetry SDK in the repository, and no remote switches or config delivery — behaviour is decided by local code and local settings alone. There is no backend server and nowhere to report to; you can build it yourself and inspect the output for any abnormal behaviour, without taking our word for it.

type=password inputs and hidden fields are skipped at isTextEditable, and that check is a whitelist: only textarea, text/search inputs and contenteditable regions are ever processed, nothing else. Both the paste-injection and the side-panel paths keep that guard in code, with no exceptions and nothing configurable around it.

Every Release ships sha256 checksums in a SHA256SUMS manifest — download it and run shasum -a 256 -c to verify the zips yourself — together with LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt; any change to the source code alters the checksum, and the Firefox submission carries a source zip cut straight from that tag.

items.q: Does it upload my text anywhere?
items.a: No. Detection and replacement run entirely on your device (service worker or side-panel memory). The only network activity in the whole repository is downloading model files, and only after you enable the AI tier yourself.

items.q: Do I have to download the AI model?
items.a: No. The regex tier is always on and covers secrets, connection strings, phone numbers, national IDs, bank cards, IBANs and other fixed-shape targets — zero latency, offline. The AI tier only adds shapeless entities like names and addresses. The quantized model is about 183 MB, downloaded once and then served from the browser cache; if it is unavailable the pipeline falls back to pure regex. Limited by model size, AI enhancement does not reliably recognise some general Chinese text (fixed-shape targets remain handled by the always-on regex tier); multilingual support is on the roadmap.

items.q: What if it flags something that is not sensitive?
items.a: Switch that row from "replace" to "keep" and it stays as-is for this run. If the same type keeps false-positiving, create a custom profile to change that type's default action, or add the value to the whitelist. Issues are welcome too — false positives are the most important problem for a tool like this.

items.q: Which sites does it work on?
items.a: The side panel does not depend on any site and always works. Paste interception requires per-site authorisation: you add a domain, the browser asks you to grant access, and only then is the listener injected. Unauthorised sites are completely untouched, and the manifest contains no content_scripts or all_urls.

items.q: Does it support rich-text editors in web pages?
items.a: Currently input[type=text/search] and textarea. contenteditable rich-text areas are not handled — paste fragments are hard to locate reliably there, and it is better to skip them than to ship a version that occasionally rewrites the wrong part.

items.q: Which interface languages are available? Do placeholders follow?
items.a: Chinese and English for now. The interface language also decides the placeholder wording: a Chinese UI produces <<手机号>>, an English UI produces <<PHONE>>. The parser accepts names from both languages, so mapping tables written before a language switch still restore correctly.

Yes — Apache-2.0 permits closed-source commercial use. The conditions are that you keep the copyright and NOTICE notices, mark your changes, and use your own name and icons; the ContextWatchdog name and icon are the author's trademark and are not covered by the code licence.

items.q: Will there be paid features later?
items.a: No. Every feature is fully enabled right now: no paid tier, no quota, no accounts. and no plans to add paywalls — the extension’s own capability panel says the same thing.

footer.static: This site is static: no client-side scripts (bar one copy button), no CDN, no third-party analytics, no web fonts.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.lead: In one sentence: we do not collect any of your data. The verifiable details are below.
privacyPage.noCollect: ContextWatchdog does not collect, upload or store any of your text or personal information. No account, no telemetry, no third-party analytics SDK.

flowRows.where: on-device (service worker or side-panel memory); never leaves your machine
on-device (WASM / ONNX Runtime); never leaves your machine
whitelisted model sources (a ModelScope mirror, falling back to huggingface.co); model files only — user data is never uploaded
per-site, stored in chrome.storage.local; unauthorised sites are never touched

privacyPage.thirdParty: The third-party components in use and their licences are listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (both inside the bundle and in the repository). The model downloaded at runtime is onnx-community/gliner_small-v2 (Apache-2.0).
privacyPage.contact: Open an issue for anything privacy-related.

entries.title: First public release
bullets: Two detection tiers: the always-on regex tier (14 categories plus algorithmic validation) and the opt-in AI tier (a local GLiNER model), sharing one dedupe and arbitration pass
Per-site paste interception: pasted text is redacted in place with placeholders and an 'N redacted' toast, across input/textarea and contenteditable
Page widget: toggle AI for the current site or open the side panel on authorised sites, with local post-paste AI upgrades
Import/exportable detection profiles, custom regex rules and allowlists, with light and dark themes following your system
Chrome and Firefox builds, bilingual UI (Simplified Chinese and English), with no account, no telemetry and no server
